issues.title: Offset-aware join filter pushdown through CM integral compress projections (min/max + BF)
issues.hypothesis: In the current best q09 plan (profile after E0002), the most expensive operator is the o_orderkey = l_orderkey HASH_JOIN at 2.22s CPU. orders (15M rows) probes a 3.27M-row build side, but only about 20% of the orders rows can match. The orders TABLE_SCAN has no dynamic filters at all because there is a PROJECTION __internal_compress_integral_uinteger(#0, 1) between the scan and the join. PushdownJoinFilterExpression (src/optimizer/join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) only passes BOUND_COLUMN_REF and integral BOUND_CAST, so GetPushdownFilterTargets bails out at that projection. Both join sides are compressed with the same offset (the build-side projection is also __internal_compress_integral_uinteger(#0/#4, 1)), so the HT keys and BF hashes are compressed uint32 values c = key - min. Hash<uint32>(c) = MurmurHash64(uint64(c)) and Hash<int64>(k) = MurmurHash64(uint64(k)) (common/types/hash.hpp:36-60), so a probe key k matches a BF entry exactly when hash(k - offset) is used. A BF on o_orderkey should cut the orders probe from 15M to about 3M rows. That removes about 12M random probes into a hash table larger than 64MB (~1.2s CPU), and the BF itself costs about 0.15s CPU.
issues.plan:
1) join_filter_pushdown.hpp: add to JoinFilterPushdownColumn an `bool has_offset=false; hugeint_t offset=0;` (or Value).
2) join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp PushdownJoinFilterExpression: add case BOUND_FUNCTION. If the function name starts with "__internal_compress_integral_", it has exactly 2 children, children[1] is a non-NULL BoundConstantExpression, filter.has_offset is false (only one level allowed), and child[0]'s type is integral with size <= 8 bytes, then set filter.offset = constant cast to HUGEINT and has_offset = true, and recurse into children[0]. Otherwise return false.
3) physical_hash_join.cpp JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (~line 832): if pushdown_column.has_offset, cast min_val and max_val to HUGEINT, add the offset, then DefaultTryCastAs(storage_type), and `continue` on failure. Skip PushInFilter when has_offset, or add the offset to each value. For the BF (line 898-901), when has_offset, treat has_cast as false if storage_type is an integral type of at most 64 bits (excluding UBIGINT/UHUGEINT) and the condition type is integral. Pass the offset into PushBloomFilter, which needs a new optional int64 offset param.
4) bloom_filter.hpp/.cpp BFTableFilter: add an `int64_t key_offset` plus a `bool has_key_offset`, kept through the constructor, Copy and Serialize (optional property). In HashInternal, when has_key_offset is set, cast the (sliced) keys to a BIGINT state vector, subtract the offset (BinaryExecutor or a simple loop, preserving validity), then call VectorOperations::Hash on that vector. FilterValue: subtract too. CheckStatistics MUST return NO_PRUNING_POSSIBLE when has_key_offset, or else apply the offset in TemplatedCheckStatistics; otherwise zone-map pruning would be wrong.
5) Check that the deferred BF path (physical_hash_join.cpp:588 PushBloomFilter at finalize) carries the offset.
Tests: join a large table against a filtered table on an integer key whose min is non-zero (e.g. keys starting at 1000), with CM active (default). Compare results to the same query with `k+0` keys. Include NULL keys and negative-min keys.
issues.expected_gain: q09: -12..-25%. The orders HJ (2.22s CPU of about 4.4s hot CPU) loses about 80% of its probe rows, and fewer rows flow through the orders compress projection.
issues.generality: This applies to any hash join where CM compresses integer keys on the probe side before the join. That is common for FK joins on integer keys with known statistics ranges, for example TPC-H/DS fact-dimension joins where the probe side is not the bottom of a pipeline under a compress projection. Min/max dynamic filters through compress projections also enable zone-map pruning. A query could get slightly slower when the BF is unselective, but the SelectivityOptionalFilter self-disables in that case.
issues.risk: Medium. The offset arithmetic and casts must be exact. CheckStatistics on a BF with an offset must not prune. Mixing signed and unsigned values: restrict to storage types up to int64/uint32. A wrong offset gives wrong results, which needs tests with a non-zero min and negative values.

issues.title: Exact key bitmap mode for join BF on dense integer build keys
issues.hypothesis: The lineitem scan carries the l_partkey BF and is the largest operator in q09 (5.28s CPU in the profile, 60M rows in, 3.27M out). The BF is sized for 436K build rows: 12 bits/key, next power of two = 8Mbit = 1MB. Each probe does a Murmur hash plus a random load into 1MB, which mostly misses L2. The build key range from min/max is 12..1999993, about 2M bits = 250KB. An exact bitmap indexed by (key - min) needs no hashing, fits L2 and has no false positives. A sibling run measured -15% on q21 with this mechanism (128 bits/key cap).
issues.plan: In BloomFilter (src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp) add an exact mode, SetKeyRange(min, range), used when the build key is integral, range <= 128 * ht count and range <= 2^31. Insert/lookup become bit set/test on (key - min). Out-of-range probes are rejected. The probe side reads the raw key values instead of hashes. In FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp ~line 901) the min/max is known, so decide the mode there before the deferred build. JoinHashTable::InsertHashes/Finalize (join_hashtable.cpp) fills the bitmap from layout column 0 instead of hashes. CheckStatistics must handle the mode.
issues.expected_gain: q09: -5..-10%, if the BF probe is a real part of the hot lineitem scan cost (unverified; cold profile).
issues.generality: Any join BF whose build keys are dense integers, which is typical for surrogate keys and FKs.
issues.risk: Medium. Two code paths in the BF, and must keep hash mode for non-integral keys. The hot gain is uncertain because an earlier decode-side tweak on this scan gave 0% hot.

output.memory:
# Memory (db_evolve, q09 specialisation run)

## Status: gen1 r3, best 1.809x (E0001 contains selectivity -29%, E0002 BF on first key of multi-key HJ -22%)

## q09 plan after E0002 (dbe-tool profile, cold-ish 1.33s total; bench hot ~552ms)
- part (contains filter, 109K) -> build; partsupp probe (BF ps_partkey) -> 436K = build side.
- lineitem scan (BF l_partkey + useless full-range min/max) 60M->3.27M, scan 5.28s CPU (cold; hot unknown),
  HJ on 2 keys 0.73s.
- That 3.27M is the build for the orders probe: orders 15M rows, NO dynamic filters (blocked by the CM proj
  __internal_compress_integral_uinteger(#0,1) on both sides). HJ 2.22s CPU = biggest operator.
- supplier⋈nation tiny; agg 0.23s; compress string proj 0.14s.

## Dispatched r3: offset-aware pushdown through CM compress projections (min/max + BF with key offset)
- Key fact: Hash<uint32>(c) == Hash<int64>(k) == MurmurHash64(uint64(v)) for 0<=v<2^32 (hash.hpp:36-60),
  so BF probe = hash(k - offset) matches build hashes of the compressed keys.
- Must make BFTableFilter::CheckStatistics not prune (or apply the offset) when an offset is set.
- If it fails on correctness, it was a bad implementation (offset/cast); the idea is sound (q18 sibling run gained -13.6% with it).

## Backlog idea: exact bitmap BF for dense int keys (q21 sibling run -15%). The lineitem l_partkey range is 2M
  bits vs a 1MB hashed BF. Uncertain hot gain: a sibling run found decode-side tweaks on the lineitem scan gave 0% hot
  (the cold profile overstates scan cost).

## Old (pre-E0001) facts
- Large-build HJs are expensive (~190-300ns/build row): random writes. Small-build HJ probed by 8M rows costs ~0.14s.
- BuildProbeSideOptimizer flip thresholds: orders join flips if left est < ~10M.

## Codebase facts
- JSON profile trick: PRAGMA enable_profiling='json'; SET profiling_output='/tmp/x.json'; run query; then
  SELECT unnest(regexp_extract_all(regexp_replace(content,'\s+',' ','g'),'"extra_info": \{[^}]*\}',0)) FROM read_text(...)
- Don't use pipes/`| grep`/cd in dbe-tool bash calls (blocked); run dbe-tool profile plain.
- Optimizer order: STATISTICS_PROPAGATION (adds CM compress projections) runs BEFORE JOIN_FILTER_PUSHDOWN.
  PushdownJoinFilterExpression (join_filter_pushdown_optimizer.cpp:23) passes only colref and integral casts;
  GetPushdownFilterTargets passes through PROJECTION/AGG groups only if every expression passes.
- JoinFilterPushdownInfo::FinalizeFilters (physical_hash_join.cpp:815): per condition it does min/max ->
  SelectivityOptionalFilter, IN filter for small HTs, and BF only if !has_cast && first key && CanUseBloomFilter
  (:761: EQUAL, build_side_has_filter, probe est > ht count, not perfect). The BF push is deferred to HT finalize (:588).
- BF (planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp): 12 bits/key, pow2 sectors of 64 bits, 4 bits per key; probe = VectorOperations::Hash + LookupHashes.
  CheckStatistics enumerates ranges <= 2048 for zone-map pruning.
- E0002: for multi-key joins the BF is filled by gathering layout col 0 in JoinHashTable::InsertHashes.

## Exhausted / retired
- Multi-key BF: DONE (E0002). Flip/contains selectivity: DONE (E0001).
